## 5. Regression tests from the failure ledger

12 of 19 recorded failure(s) name a regression test.

Without one: FAIL-002 (The failing environment is a system Python with no tree-sitter; reproducing it in a test means altering the interpreter. Verified by hand with a plain ./omni graph build, the no-venv path and a failing OMNI_GRAPH_PYTHON.), FAIL-003 (Needs WSL and a Windows browser. The page itself was checked for JS errors at three window sizes in headless Chromium; a real Windows Chrome was not available.), FAIL-010 (A dedicated regression test would need a YAML-parsing dependency (PyYAML), which this project's own test suite deliberately avoids to stay stdlib-only; PyYAML isn't guaranteed present on a fresh clone. Prevention is process instead: validate any workflow edit with a local YAML parse before pushing (now done for this fix and noted for next time).), FAIL-012 (A repository-state defect (a committed output directory), not a code path: the fix is the untracking and the ignore entry, which git enforces from now on.), FAIL-016 (A workflow file has no unit test; Arbiter's supply.unpinned-action rule in the self-gate is the check that catches a return to tags.), FAIL-017 (The defect is a timing race in test teardown; the fix removes the background process rather than asserting on it.), FAIL-018 (A timing race in test teardown; the fix removes the background process rather than asserting on it, as for FAIL-017.).
